INTRODUCTION
CREDITS
4
Introduction

The Revolt of Mallobaude is a two-player campaign supplement set during the prelude to the End Times. It can be played independently or alongside the other End Times supplements, allowing you to replay - and perhaps alter - the final days of the Warhammer world.

This volume is not self-contained. Use it alongside the companion Game Guide, which describes the course of the campaign independently of the rules system used to play it.

This volume contains all the rules needed to play the campaign with Warhammer Fantasy Battles 8th Edition.

It introduces new characters, units, and army lists representing the forces that fought during the Revolt of Mallobaude. They can be used both in the campaign and in other games of Warhammer.

Most of these game elements can be reused outside the campaign. The rules are modular, so you may use them separately or combine them as you wish.

This is an unofficial supplement, so agree with your opponents before using it. You are also free to alter any part of it if doing so improves your gaming experience.

Credits

The source texts used in this volume are drawn from Warhammer: Nagash; Warhammer Armies: Wood Elves and Warhammer Armies: Bretonnia (all © Games Workshop); and Knights of the Grail and Barony of the Damned for Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay, 2nd Edition (both © Black Industries).

Some rules are taken from Warhammer Armies: Wood Elves, 5th Edition; Warhammer Armies: Bretonnia, 6th Edition; Warhammer Armies: Vampire Counts, 8th Edition; and Warhammer: Thanquol. Part of the Civil War article published in White Dwarf is also reproduced here. All are © Games Workshop and appear without authorisation.

The illustrations come from numerous publications and are © Games Workshop unless otherwise noted. Artists are credited wherever possible. Most images were originally published on the artist's website or the Games Workshop website rather than scanned from a printed work.

Additional text was written by Dreadaxe, Ilmarith, Kass-Krâne, and Thindaraïel, in alphabetical order. The supplement was developed on the WarFo at warhammer-forum.com in the “WFB Creation and Development” section. Many other participants contributed along the way; there are too many to list here, but we thank them all for their help.

Characters and Units represent forces that
distinguished themselves during the End
Times, but you can reuse them in other
battles, with the agreement of your
opponent.
We hope you find this supplement useful
to enhance your Warhammer games.

HOW TO USE THIS SUPPLEMENT
5
How to Use This Supplement

This rules supplement focuses on the Revolt of Mallobaude. It contains:

Civil War Rules: Adapted from the official rules published in White Dwarf, these allow battles between armies chosen from the same army book - in this campaign, Bretonnia and Vampire Counts.

New Units and Characters: Rules are provided for Mallobaude, every Bretonnian duke alive at the time of the End Times, several famous Undead, a handful of Wood Elf heroes, and variants of the Green Knight and King Louen Leoncoeur reflecting their development during the campaign.

New Armies: The book includes combined army lists such as the Mousillon Army and the Alliance Against Undeath, together with restricted lists representing specific forces such as the Crusade Army and the Wildwood Host.

Narrative Scenarios: These scenarios recreate the campaign's defining battles in games of Warhammer.

How to Use These Rules

Like the official End Times books, this supplement is a toolbox from which you can select material for any game of Warhammer. Some scenarios require particular characters or units, but they can readily be adapted using different models or armies. The armies, characters, and units represent forces that fought during the End Times, but may also be used in other battles with your opponent's agreement.

We hope this supplement enriches your games of Warhammer.

Required Supplements

These rules are not entirely self-contained. The following official and unofficial supplements are required:

Army books

  • Vampire Counts, 8th Edition
  • Tomb Kings, 8th Edition
  • The Empire, 8th Edition
  • Wood Elves, 8th Edition
  • High Elves, 8th Edition
  • Bretonnia, 6th Edition, with its 8th Edition compatibility FAQ

Supplements

  • Triumph & Treachery
  • Blood in the Badlands
  • The End Times: Glottkin

CAMPAIGN RULES
BRETONNIAN RULES
6
Campaign Rules

The following campaign rules appear here rather than in the Game Guide because their effects depend on the rules system being used.

The Kingdom Without a King: The Loyalists are demoralised by the loss of the King. They suffer a -1 penalty to their Leadership for all Leadership tests.

Teeming Ranks: Mallobaude's legions are reinforced by the fresh corpses of the war's victims. A Mousillon army may include one unit of Zombies worth up to 200 points for each Necromancer or Master Necromancer in the army, including Arkhan and Kemmler.

Bretonnian Rules

The following Bretonnian terrain rules add character to the battlefield. They are taken from, or inspired by, Storm of Magic.

Chapel of the Lady
Many altars and chapels dedicated to the Lady stand upon the sites of heroic battles or over the graves of Grail Knights.

Building. A model belonging to the Chaos or Death alliance must re-roll successful ward saves while within 6" of an Altar or Chapel of the Lady. A Bretonnian unit occupying the Altar or Chapel has the Unbreakable special rule for as long as it remains there.

Pure Water Spring
The Lady of the Lake's sacred power can be felt in every clear pond and stream.

River. A Wizard within 6" of a Pure Water Spring may roll up to four dice when channelling instead of only one. If three or more of those dice roll a 6, immediately roll on the Miscast table. In addition, any unit within 3" of the spring has the Regeneration (5+) special rule.

For this campaign, every Damsel or Prophetess, including the Fay Enchantress, knows the following spell in addition to her normal spells.

Curse of the Lady - Cast on 12+

Casting aside the tattered remnants of virtue and nobility, the Damsel calls down the Lady's wrath upon those champions who dare oppose Bretonnia.

Hex. The spell targets a single enemy character within 12". The target must immediately pass a Leadership test with a -3 modifier or be transformed into a toad. Models belonging to the Chaos or Death alliance must re-roll successful tests, while Bretonnian models may re-roll failed tests.

While transformed, the model cannot channel or cast spells. Its magic items and other equipment have no effect, and all its characteristics are reduced to 1 except for its Wounds.

At the start of each of the controlling player's subsequent Magic phases, roll a D6 for every transformed model. On a 4+, the spell ends and the model returns to its normal form. Mounts are unaffected.

CIVIL WAR
7
Civil War

Note: These rules are adapted from the Civil War rules published in the French monthly edition of White Dwarf, issues 213-216, between January and April 2012. Only the rules needed for The Revolt of Mallobaude campaign are reproduced here.

For this campaign, ignore the Faction rule from the original expansion. It was intended to make armies more thematic, but does not suit the structure of this campaign.

In a Civil War, armies chosen from the same army book clash. Because both sides use many of the same rules, Jervis Johnson created a set of simple tables to add uncertainty and variety to the battle. These rules do not alter army selection, so no advance preparation is required.

Before the battle, roll once on two of the following tables. The first table is used by every army. The other two are specific to Bretonnia and Vampire Counts; the campaign or scenario rules specify which one to use.

2D6Civil War Battle Table
2

Annihilation

The only way this dispute will be resolved is by the complete destruction of the other side.

All units in both armies are Unbreakable. Ignore the normal rules for Game Length and Victory Conditions. Instead, the game lasts until one side is completely destroyed; the surviving side wins.

3

Lust for Battle

The troops in both armies are desperate to get to grips with each other.

All units in both armies have the Vanguard special rule.

4

Pent-Up Fury

The two sides are seething with pent-up aggression.

All units in both armies have the Devastating Charge special rule.

5

Undeserving

Each side considers the other unworthy to carry the battle standards under which they march.

The Victory Points for Seized Standards increase to 100 points for each slain standard bearer and 500 points for the enemy Battle Standard Bearer.

6

We Will Not Yield

Neither side is willing to back away from this fight.

All units in both armies are Stubborn.

7

Ancient Enmity

The two sides have harboured numerous grudges against each other for centuries.

Roll twice on this table, re-rolling any further rolls of 7 or duplicate results.

8

Hated Rivals

The two generals despise each other.

Each Army General Hates the opposing Army General and wins the battle immediately if that rival is slain. If both Generals are slain at exactly the same time, the battle is a draw.

9

Bloody Feud

The two sides have been feuding for years.

All units in both armies Hate all units in the other army.

10

Unreasoning Spite

Both sides are so blinded by hate that they have lost all reason.

All units in both armies are subject to Frenzy.

11

We Shall Not Yield

Both rival armies believe completely in the justness of their cause.

All units in both armies are Immune to Psychology.

12

Guerrilla War

The two sides have been ravaging each other's lands in a vicious guerrilla war.

Up to three units in each army may have the Ambushers special rule if their commander wishes.

2

Favours of the Lady

Will the Lady favour her sons?

The first time a unit is called upon to make a ward save granted by the Blessing of the Lady, it must also take a Leadership test. If the test is passed, all ward saves the unit receives from the Blessing are improved by 1.

3

Thoroughbreds

All Warhorses, Pegasi, and Royal Pegasi have +1 Strength.

4

As a Token of My Esteem

A handkerchief, scarf, or ribbon tied around a knight's lance or armour may have miraculous effects.

Each player may choose one magic item from the Bretonnian magic items list and give it to a Hero or Lord in their army, following the normal rules for magic items. If the bearer is slain in close combat by another character, the slayer automatically takes the item.

5

The True King

Claimants to the throne are all too common, and only the army's great standard proves the General's right to command.

If the Battle Standard Bearer is slain, every unit in that army must take a Panic test.

6

Duel to the Death

Before the battle, a hero from each army is chosen to represent their side in a duel of honour.

Before the game begins, each player nominates one Lord or Hero. Place the two characters in base contact at the centre of the battlefield; they fight normally in the next Close Combat phase. No other model may interfere, and both characters are Unbreakable. The victor causes Terror for the rest of the battle.

7

Ancient Enmity

The two sides have harboured numerous grudges against each other for centuries.

Roll twice on this table, re-rolling any further rolls of 7 or duplicate results.

8

Valour

Every knight is determined to enter into legend.

Whenever a character slays an enemy in a challenge, compare their points values. If the slain model was worth more points than the victor, the victor's side scores 100 Victory Points. If the battle does not use Victory Points, take comfort that the hero's deed will be celebrated throughout the land!

9

The Jacquerie

The peasants rise in revolt and refuse to bend to the nobility's will.

Units with the Peasant's Duty special rule cannot use the Leadership of a nearby knight, but gain Frenzy and Stubborn.

10

For the Glory of the Damsels

Magic floods the realm, invigorating the powers of its Damsels and Prophetesses.

Whenever a Damsel or Prophetess casts a spell, add D6 to the casting total. This additional die can cause a miscast as normal.

11

Lances of Heroes

The blood of Gilles le Breton runs in the veins of his sons!

Knights of any type re-roll To Wound rolls of 1 in a turn in which they charge.

12

The Grail

Place a marker representing the Grail at the centre of the battlefield. A Knight unit or character with any vow other than the Grail Vow that moves into contact with the marker must stop and drink. Take a Leadership test: if failed, the unit or character has Stupidity for the rest of the battle; if passed, replace its current vow with the Grail Vow. Only one unit or character may drink each turn. If an enemy unit is in contact with the Grail, it must first be destroyed or made to flee.

2D6Vampire Counts Civil War Table
2

Night of Ghosts

The fabled Geistnacht falls but once every seven years, when the spirits of the dead rise across the realm to do battle amongst their own.

Roll a D6 for each of your characters and units. On a 6, that character or unit gains the Ethereal special rule. If an Ethereal character or unit rolls a 6, however, it loses Ethereal as its members coalesce into solid ectoplasm!

3

Grasping Graves

The concentration of Dark Magic causes those in shallow graves to reach up and drag the living down among them.

At the end of each Magic phase, the player whose turn it is may nominate one enemy unit. Every model in that unit must pass a Strength test or be slain, with no saves of any kind allowed. A unit can be nominated only once per battle.

4

Lords of Bone

The skeletons raised from these lands have fossilised or petrified, hardening their ancient bones.

All Skeleton Warriors, Black Knights, Grave Guard, and Wight Kings in both armies have +1 Toughness.

5

Necrarch Relic Hunters

The ancient brotherhood of the Necrarchs has sent agents to recover the treasures of its rivals.

All Wizards have one additional Wizard level, to a maximum of 4. If a character defeats another character in a challenge, roll a D6 for each of the defeated foe's magic items. On a 4+, the victor takes that item and may use it for the rest of the battle, provided it has not been used up and is otherwise available to that character.

6

The Grand Hunt of Strigos

The troglodyte Strigoi clan is out in force, desperate to claw its way back into ascendancy.

Crypt Ghouls and Crypt Horrors have Hatred.

7

Ancient Enmity

The two sides have harboured numerous grudges against each other for centuries.

Roll twice on this table, re-rolling any further rolls of 7 or duplicate results.

8

The Iron Fist of the von Carsteins

The von Carstein family exerts its fell powers upon those who dare challenge its rule.

All von Carsteins, Vargheists, Fell Bats, Bat Swarms, and Black Coaches have +1 Strength.

9

Lahmia Ascendant

The royal sisterhood of the Lahmians reveals itself, striking at the heart of rival Vampire armies.

All female Vampires in both armies gain the Quickblood and Beguile Vampiric Powers. In addition, Pallid Handmaidens have +1 Strength.

10

Sons of Abhorash

The Blood Dragons rise in force, their honour demanding that they slay the lesser bloodlines.

Each player may field up to five Blood Knights in addition to their usual army, provided the models are available; they must form a separate unit. Roll a D6 for each male Vampire. On a 4+, he belongs to the Ordo Draconis and gains the Dread Knight and Master Strike Vampiric Powers.

11

Animus Morti

The air crackles with Necromantic power, hastening the dead to battle.

All Undead units may march regardless of their proximity to the General. In addition, every Wizard knows Vanhel's Danse Macabre; if a Wizard generates that spell normally, it counts as a duplicate.

12

Night of Dark Wings

The storm clouds are heavy with Dark Magic, strengthening the Undead creatures able to drink from them.

All units with the Fly special rule have +1 Strength and +1 Initiative, including the riders of flying mounts.

VICTOR'S REWARDS
11
Victor's Rewards

The winner of each battle chooses one of the following rewards. Rewards may be combined - for example, two Ancient Relics may be used in the same battle. Once used, a reward is spent and cannot be used again in a later battle.

Command from On High (Common): The supreme commander - Louen or Mallobaude - orders his forces to ignore a needless battle, leaving the enemy to find an empty field. Use this reward to avoid one battle at stage 2, 6, 8, or 10. Your opponent is treated as the victor and gains a reward, but you suffer no penalty for losing a Duke.

Challenge of Authority (Common): Use this reward when one of your characters is within 8" of an enemy character who has a Chivalric Virtue or Vampiric Power. Your character issues a resounding challenge, which the enemy must accept. From that point, either designated character may move in the Movement phase only if the move brings them closer together; any move that increases the distance between them is forbidden. Random Movement is unaffected. Once they are in base contact, the two characters are automatically placed in a challenge during the Close Combat phase, and neither may refuse. The challenger gains a +2 combat result bonus if they defeat their opponent.

Unexpected Reinforcements (Bretonnia): Prepare an additional unit worth no more than 150 points before the battle, but keep it secret. It may enter play from turn 3 onwards, from any table edge that touches your original deployment zone. If the deployment zone touches no table edge, as in a Last Stand, it may enter from any edge. The unit arrives after charges are declared and may make a full move.

Favour of the Lady (Bretonnia): For this battle, you have 1+D3 re-rolls. Each may be used on any dice roll, such as a Break test, To Hit roll, saving throw, or casting roll.

Ancient Relic (Common): Before deployment, give one of your characters a magic item worth up to 75 points at no cost.

Blood Kiss (Mousillon): A young noble has received the Blood Kiss and joins the ranks of the accursed. At the start of the battle, choose one enemy champion or character with the Knight's Vow; named characters cannot be chosen. A champion is transformed into a Blood Knight champion on a 4+, a Hero into a Vampire Thrall on a 5+, or a Lord into a Vampire Lord on a 6+. If the roll fails, the victim resists the Kiss or overcomes the attacker. A transformed model retains all its magic equipment and receives an Undead equivalent of its original mount. It joins the Mousillon army as an independent character, even if it began the battle as a champion.

Nocturnal Summoning (Mousillon): The Necromancers have laboured through the night to draw fresh corpses from nearby graves. Immediately before the battle, add 2+D6 Skeletons or Zombies, or 1+D3 cavalry models, to an existing unit at no cost.

Nexus of Death (Mousillon): The Undead general has manoeuvred the foe into battle near a site that draws Death magic. Before deployment, the Rebel player may place two Sylvanian terrain features from Warhammer: Nagash - Book I in their half of the battlefield at no cost.

Duke Armand of Aquitaine
Duke Armand of Aquitaine was one of the
younger brothers of the previous Duke and
he did not expect to inherit. As a Knight
Errant, he was renowned for both his
recklessness and his luck, and he refused all
offers of a fiefdom until King Louen himself
offered him a place in the royal household.
Once again, Armand distinguished himself
by his prowess, particularly by defeating
the Bestigor Darmal the Hooked in single
combat. Many expected him to be given a
Barony and made a Marquess.
Instead, after just two years, he left on a
Quest for the Grail. He left incognito, and
did not speak of his activities after his
return. A few minstrels attempted to gather
information about his doings, but he was
not the only Questing Knight to have
concealed his identity. Upon his return, as a
Grail
Knight,
he
was
appointed
standard-bearer of Bretonnia, a position
that suited him well.
Duke Adalhard of Lyonesse
Duke Adalhard de Lyonesse was a simple
man. He excelled on the battlefield, and off
it, he enjoyed feasting, gambling, and other
warrior pastimes. Some observers have
suggested from his style that his true
loyalty was to Ulric, not the Lady of the
Lake. They put this fact down to the Norse
blood which flows in the veins of the
Lyonesses of the north.
The Duke stayed away from the politics of
the duchy as much as possible. If a conflict
grew too large for him to continue ignoring,
he would bring in his troops, crush all
opposing parties, seize their lands, and
declare the matter resolved. This method
In 2519, the old Duke of Aquitaine died in
battle while intervening in one of the
duchy's endless blood feuds. Four of his
sons had died before him, and the youngest
was simple-minded and was kept locked
up. However, he also had two daughters
and they would normally have inherited
from him. The King chose to ignore them
and grant the dukedom to Armand. He had
to find his feet as an administrator; he was
eager to solve problems personally and by
force.
Grateful to the King, to whom he devoted
absolute loyalty, Armand remained guided
by his impulsiveness and by an intense
sense of honour. It is these qualities and
these
faults
that
led
him
to
face
Mallobaude, and to meet on the battlefield
the fate of all imprudent people.
Armand of Aquitaine is a Bretonnian Lord,
who has taken the Grail Vow, endowed
with the Virtue of Knightly Temper
and riding a barded warhorse. You can
choose his other options.
proved effective every time he used it, and
the nobles tried hard to plot without
attracting the attention of their overlord.
After the disappearance of the Fay Enchantress
Mallobaude's emissaries were quick
to convince Adélard that the Grail was only
a lie. The Duke then joined the insurgents,
and only recognized his error during his
agony, after King Louen had mortally

Adalhard of Lyonesse is a Bretonnian Lord,

Duke Tancred II of Quenelles
Duke Tancred II has proven himself to be
an excellent lord for Quenelles. He had his
moment of glory when he defeated the
Necromancer Heinrich Kemmler and the
Undead Chaos Champion Krell, who had
allied with the Skaven and attacked
Maisontaal Abbey. But it was in 1513 (2491
C.I.) and the Duke was at the time of the
Mallobaude revolt an old man, stooped
and diminished, although he still had good
remnants of his former vigor.
Tancred, well aware that he was going to
die, worried about the future of the duchy.
He had had four sons, all dead or missing,
and the Quenelles inheritance seemed
very compromised. The final decision
rested with the King, but Duke Tancred
hoped to appoint a successor during his
lifetime.
Duke Alberic of Bordeleaux
Duke Alberic of Bordeleaux was famous for
his
personal
courage
and
incredible
self-discipline. We also know that he
expected the Knights of his household to
adhere to the same rigor and that he
dismissed those who did not do so. As a
result, his house was the smallest in
strength among all the Dukes, but his
Knights were among the best in the entire
kingdom.
The Duke always wanted to go on the Grail
Quest, but his father had died while he was
wandering and Alberic never felt able to
entrust responsibility for the duchy to
anyone else. But with his eldest son,
Frermund, having himself undertaken his
own Grail Quest, the aging Alberic began
looking for a steward to manage the duchy in
his absence when the Civil War broke out.

Duke Huebald of Carcassonne
Duke
Huebald
of
Carcassonne
was
relatively small, thin and lively rather than
powerful. He only spoke when it was
necessary, and even then, remained as
concise as possible. No one around him
had ever seen him smile, let alone laugh.
His union with his wife Schermilde was a
political marriage and the fact that the
couple had four children, all of whom came
from
the
Duke,
was
a
matter
of
astonishment. However, the Duke was
respected by all his men. He was the best
war leader the Gasconnais had had for
generations and a courageous warrior to
boot. Unlike many Bretonnian Knights, he
was willing to use ambushes and feints to
defeat his monstrous adversaries. He
claimed that the greenskins who came
down from the mountains to burn villages
did not deserve to be fought honourably.
Duke Bohemond of Bastonne
Duke Bohemond of Bastonne was a Grail
Knight particularly famous for fighting
monsters, so much so that he was
nicknamed “the Bane of Beasts”. He was
also known for refusing to fight inferior
opponents, even if they attacked him. He
would just knock them out and turn his
attention elsewhere. When his fame grew,
he traveled to many places in Bretonnia
and beyond to find suitable adversaries.
Although Bohemond was a descendant of
the line of Gilles le Breton, he showed
absolute loyalty to King Louen and had no
desire to seize the crown. In fact, he
affected power so little that he delegated
the administration of his duchy to his
Steward, and matters of justice to his
Grand Justiciar. Unfortunately, he had
little ability to judge the character of others
and he had to replace these men at an
alarming rate.
Although he used deception, Huebald
could not stand it being used on him. Also
when Mallobaude told him his “truth”
about the Lady of the Lake, Huebald flew
into a rage, matching Mallobaude’s fury
when the latter had his revelation. The two
men were subsequently closely linked,
until the premature death of the Duke
during the battle between him and the
King's forces.

Duke Folcard of Montfort
Duke Folcard of Montfort was something
of an anomaly among the Dukes of
Bretonnia. He was a formidable warrior,
but he almost never fought on horseback.
The mountains that cover his duchy
seriously handicap mounted fighters, and
the Duke could tolerate no delay in his fight
against the Greenskins whose lands were
infested before the arrival of Chaos.
Duke Folcard was perhaps the Bretonnian
nobleman most beloved by his subjects. He
seemed to sincerely care about the peasant
villages and tried to help them when they
were under attack from raiders. He set up
a network of lanterns to communicate in
the mountains, which allowed relief troops
to arrive on time in most cases, and he
15
Duke Taubert de L’Anguille
Duke Taubert of L'Anguille was a sailor in
his youth, but he neither set foot on a ship
nor lived within sight of the sea for more
than fifteen years after his last sea
expedition. He confided the reasons to no
one. After his return, Duke Taubert settled
at Grasgar Castle, on the edge of the Forest
of Arden, a castle that the Dukes had used
as a hunting lodge for generations, but
Duke Taubert had it enlarged and used it
as a base for his expeditions into the heart
of the forest. He claimed his goal was to
defeat the Beastmen, but many believed he
simply wanted to stay as far from the sea
as possible.
Because of his absence, the Duke was
unknown to most of the townspeople in
the port of L'Anguille. Among the peasants
in the countryside, things were very
different. To them, the Duke was a hero
who fought the Beastmen himself. He built
a series of watchtowers all around the
forest, which raised the alarm at Grasgar
Castle when bands of raiders were spotted.
Armed troops were then sent, often led
Duke Cassyon of Parravon
Duke Cassyon of Parravon was the
youngest Duke of Bretonnia at the time of
the Civil War, being just over twenty years
old. Regardless, he was a Grail Knight and
he rode a Royal Pegasus. His father died
while Cassyon was on his Grail Quest and
the young Duke did not know of his
status until returning to Parravon.
The
Duke's
advisors
found
him
exasperating. He was an open and
enthusiastic young man, who had no ill
will towards anyone, which made him
impossible to hate. On the other hand, he
thought he could fulfill his duty as Duke
by simply riding the skies above his duchy
and slaughtering monsters. He was quite
gifted in this
by the Duke himself. More than one
village
was
saved
from
absolute
destruction by the timely arrival of the
Duke's men, and he himself saved the
lives of some of his subjects, which
greatly improved their opinion of him.
In the years before the End Times, the
Beastmen grew increasingly cunning, and
the more brutal herds turned their attention
to Lyonesse, Artois, and Couronne. This
caused tensions with the surrounding
duchies and some nobles muttered that
Duke Taubert would have done better to
defeat the Beastmen rather than drive
them back to the lands of other lords.

protecting this monastery that he met his

Theodoric of Brionne is a Bretonnian Lord
who has taken the Knight's Vow and carries
a great weapon. He also has the special rule
Frenzy, which adds an additional cost of
+10 points. You may choose his other options.
Duke Chilfroy of Artois
Duke Chilfroy of Artois was an immense
man, stronger and more robust than any of
his Knights or nobles. He was also famous
for his austerity: no one ever heard him
laugh and it was claimed that he only
smiled at the devastation he sowed among
his enemies. While he wasn't very subtle,
he was a great warlord when the strategies
were simple and those who followed him
only needed a little motivation.
The Duke spent most of his time hunting
monsters, Beastmen and other creatures
from the depths of the Forest of Arden.
The great hall of the Château d'Artois was
decorated with stuffed heads and furs
from his greatest victories. This is where
he held his court of justice. He was known
for settling cases quickly by declaring the
higher-ranking plaintiff in the right and
meting out brutal punishment to the loser.
As a result,
Duke Theodoric of Brionne
Duke Theodoric of Brionne sometimes
seemed to have a split personality. In
battle, he was a true terror, swinging his
great battle ax with deadly efficiency. He
cut down terrifying enemies, leaving their
corpses to the cold earth. He was always on
the front lines guiding his troops and he
rarely returned without injury. Among his
Knights, it was rumored that a spirit of war
had taken possession of him, for he
seemed
to
take
great
pleasure
in
massacres.
Far from the battlefield, the Duke was a
protector of the arts, connoisseur of music
and singing. He was the greatest patron of
the minstrels of Bretonnia and listened
attentively to their love stories. There

Mallobaude one day had a vision of the Lady that
changed his life. From a Questing Knight,
piously searching the paths for the path that
would lead him to the Lady of the Lake, he
became the fiercest of his adversaries, determined
to exterminate the cult of the Lady.
The army he assembles is disparate, and
will be even more so after the revelation
that he has become a vampire, but certain
rules are common to these two armies and
to various characters. You will find them
gathered here for greater simplicity.
The Black Grail Vow Those closest to
Mallobaude are called the Knights of
the Black Grail, obsessed with the
Black Grail that Mallobaude presented
to them. Subsequently, Mallobaude
would later lead them into undeath.
This oath replaces the Grail Vow. The
Oath of the Black Grail grants an
ward save of 6+, as well as the
fear rule. The Grail result in the
Civil War table is considered the Black
Grail for Rebels who drink from it,
granting them the Black Grail
Vow.

the

(including

bearing the Grail Vow and the Grail
Pilgrims. Standard of Mousillon

an

of

of

Legend has it that it carries

THE REBELS OF BRETONNIA
SORCERERS
Mallobaude's army includes none of the Lady's witches, but it
attracts Sorcerers - self-taught practitioners who manipulate
unstable energies. Use the points costs and profiles for
Wizards and Wizard Lords in Warhammer Armies: The
Empire, but note that they cannot take any mount other than a
warhorse. They use the Lores of Shadow, Fire, Death, or Beasts
and gain one free power die when casting. However, they roll
one extra die on the Miscast table and keep the two lowest.
BLACK GRAIL KNIGHTS
These are Grail Knights who have taken the Black Grail Vow.
After Mallobaude is revealed as a vampire, the Black Grail
Knights forming the elite of the Mousillon army use the
separate rules on page 24.
ROGUES
Naturally, no Grail Pilgrim can join Mallobaude's army, but
its ranks are full of unsavory individuals, wayward pilgrims,
and common brigands. Represent them using Militia from
the Empire army list.

During the Revolt of Mallobaude, Arkhan the
Black was present, initially hidden in the shadow of the
renegade he advised, and later openly as lieutenant to
Mallobaude.
In reality, Arkhan manipulated Mallobaude. He cared little
whether Leoncoeur's son took the throne; what mattered was
the ruin and devastation of the civil war, which would
give him the chance to attack La Maisontaal and seize the
artefact preserved there.
Use Arkhan the Black's rules from the
Tomb Kings army book (do not use the Mortarch
version from Warhammer: Nagash - Book II),
except for the following:
Arkhan cannot take a Skeleton Chariot during
this campaign. Replace his Undead rule from
Nehekhara with the Undead rule from the
Vampire Counts army book. Ignore the Liche
High Priest and Tomb King unit types.
Arkhan does not count as a hierophant, since
he is not used here in a Tomb Kings army.
However,
he
counts
as
a
Master
Necromancer. Arkhan can use the Lore of the
Vampires and spells from the Lore of Undeath
instead of the Lore of Death. He has the
Master of the Dead option for necromancers
for free.

Among the protagonists of this war, some had a murky role. It might have initially been thought that
they would side with one side or the other, but in fact they followed their own plans, and further added
to the chaos of this confrontation. Ideally, these armies should be played by a third player
Drycha fought for centuries to free her lord Coeddil, one of the last and oldest
Treeman Ancients, a witness to the birth of the world. Coeddil, locked by Ariel deep in the Wild Woods,
had gone mad and hated the Asrai. His servant Drycha and all the spirits who accompanied her
shared the same hatred. Drycha led an army of vengeful spirits to capture the Fay Enchantress,
daughter of Corrygil the elf goddess of the Mists. This idea had been whispered to her by a voice in
the back of her mind, a nightmare in the middle of her dreams of revenge:

Kurnoth Hunters, © Games Workshop
Kurnous
represents
the
wildness
and
appetite of nature. The Kurnoth Hunters
are the embodiments of his anger. Almost
twice the size of a Dryad, masters of sword,
bow and scythe, they are strong enough to
break a Chaos warrior in two and tough
enough to endure the worst blows. Agile,
graceful and stoic, they do not share the
capricious nature of their kin; they focus
on their task, calm as old oaks, and deeply
invested in their fight. The Hunters of
Kurnous are the elite of the war-groves, Free
Spirits who fight under the direct orders of
the leader of their kin. Strong, agile, and
extraordinarily skilled in combat, these
warrior
spirits
embody
the
power
of
Kurnous, the hunter god, with every arrow
and every backhand of their sword, felling
their foes with frightening efficiency.
A unit of Treekin can be upgraded to
Kurnoth Hunters for +3 points per
model. You cannot have more units of
Kurnoth Hunters than Treekin.
An Ancient Treekin has the profile and cost of an Ancient Treekin but acts like a
character. He has a free Scaly Skin (3+). He can carry a heavy weapon (+6 points), a
scythe (halberd, +6 points) or a longbow (+6 points). He can have Quiverlings (+6 points).

If it does not have an Aspect, a unit of
- Dryads can be promoted to Spirit
Dryads for +5 points/model.
The most evil wood spirits form Drycha's
privileged guard. Their spiritual form
seems to emerge from their sylvan
envelope, their simple touch chilling the
blood of the living.
A dark reflection of the noble households,
the bulk of the Wildwood Host is
made up of Spirit Dryads who constantly
scream their maddening cacophony, cover
themselves in the blood of their enemies
and commit acts of nameless savagery.
Their gaze burns with absolute madness
and unspeakable hatred, while they
dance, fangs bared, slashing at the enemy
with their cruel claws. While other forest
spirits are graceful and imbued with life
magic, Spirit Dryads are terrors from the
depths of a nightmare. Shadow and light
flash around these ghostly creatures as
they bite and claw at their victims,
carving to pieces those who do not drop
their weapons and flee at the sight of
them.

Druidic practitioners of sacred life magic,
protectors of their clan's soul-seed glades,
Branchwyches are held in high esteem for
their abilities as generals and advisors in
witchcraft. It is up to them to carry out the
grim task of harvesting the seed of their
fallen comrades, which reinforces their
propensity
for
anger,
and
their
astonishing ferocity when they are angry.
The Branchwyches are accompanied by
their bittergrubs, voracious creatures
whose mandibles tear easily through flesh
and bone. Fearsome warrior matriarchs
of
the
Sylvaneth
Houses,
the
Branchwyches guide their kin into battle
with the explosions of their magic and the
whistles of their scythes. At the end of
battle, these same weapons are used to
harvest the lamentiri of those who have
fallen, thus preserving the memories and
souls of the forest spirits.

SPITE-REVENANTS
Spite-Revenants are particularly aggressive Wildwood
spirits, which is why they readily join a Spirit Host.
Use the Spirit Host rules from the Vampire Counts army
book, replacing the Undead special rule with Forest
Spirit.
29
In 1454 IC (or in 476 according to the
Bretonnian
Calendar)
the
Duke
of
Aquitaine returned from the Crusades,
transformed into a Vampire. Renamed the
Red Duke, he embarked on a campaign of
conquest across the western provinces of
Bretonnia. His reputation grew, both as a
ruthless
killer
and
an
incomparable
swordsman.
While
many
Bretonnians
cursed him for the first reason, many
rallied to his colours because of the second.
His campaign of destruction came to an
end when he was killed by the King of
Bretonnia, also Duke of Aquitaine, at the
Battle of Ceren. Almost five hundred years
later, in 1932 IC, the Red Duke emerged from
his grave. Immediately, a bloody shadow
spread over Aquitaine as he burned the
villages and slaughtered their inhabitants by
the thousands, tracing a bloody trail to the
Duke of the time in order to exact his
murderous revenge against him. The
Knights of Bretonnia gathered again to
repel the terrible threat, but this time they
failed to slay him. With what remained of
his troops, he took refuge in the Forest of
Châlons,
attacking
all
travellers
and
preparing his next attack.
No one knows why the Red Duke seemed so
intent on slaughtering the Bretonnians, but
there was much speculation. According to
some, he is a former knight who was the
victim of great injustice and wrongly
disinherited a long time ago. Others
claimed that he was the evil alter ego of the
Green Knight, the great champion of the
Lady, and that he was there to test the
weapons and the hearts of the knights of
the Grail. Whatever the truth, many knights
set out on their quest to find him and put
an end to his evil actions once and for all.
Few were able to find him, and of those who
did, none returned.
During the Revolt of Mallobaude, the
Red Duke was upset by the appearance of
this new vampire, who jeopardized the
plans he had been hatching for a long time.
The Red Duke was such an embarrassment
to Arkhan that he took up arms against
him. After his defeat, the Duke fled to
Sylvania where all trace of him was lost for some
time.
The Red Duke, © Black Library
The Red Duke is a Vampire Lord, wearing
the Blade of Leaping Gold (See High Elf
Army Book), heavy armour, riding a
barded Nightmare, and using the
Lore of the
Vampires.
He
possesses
the
vampiric powers Dread Knight and Red
Fury. In addition, he has the following
rule for an additional cost of +50 points:
Former Duke of Aquitaine The Red
Duke was once a brave Bretonnian
knight. He still uses the martial
tactics he loved during his lifetime.
Any Cavalry or Monstrous Cavalry
unit joined by the Red Duke can
adopt the Lance Formation.

The Banshee follows the usual Banshee
rules. She also benefits from the following
rules, for an additional cost of +50 points:
Hover The Banshee floats above
the ground, carried by the black
winds of necromantic magic. She
has the Hover special rule.
White Witch The Banshee has the
unique ability to cast spells. The
Banshee is a level 1 wizard using
Lore of Death or Necromancy.
Sir Falk of Castle Reces was once a
powerful knight in the service of King
Louis, until he murdered a Damsel of the
Lady out of jealousy. His retainers burned his
castle to the foundations, but his armour
survived,
horribly
blackened,
and
animated by his fierce will. Thereafter,
the Dark Knight became the captain and
herald of the undead Host in the service of
the Red Duke, condemned to fight
eternally in the ranks of the dead. Far
more powerful than most of the Wights
that infested the world, he was as arrogant
and self-confident in death as he was in
life.
The Banshee was a powerful spectre, a
malevolent creature that infested the lands
of Bretonnia for centuries. Her very
presence struck terror into the hearts of
mortals who dared to face her, and his
deathly scream, drawing its power from
the darkest magics, brought only death
and despair to those who heard it. When
the Red Duke first rose, the winds of magic
drew the Banshee into the service of the
vampire lord.

aware that the presence of an undead kingdom at the gates of Athel Loren would be a danger to

battle of Quenelles to offer help from the Fay Folk and agree on a common strategy.

Ariel is the Queen of Athel Loren
and presides over the kingdom
with Orion. Ariel acquired the
Aspects of Isha, the ancient elven
goddess of nature, through the
strange magic of the Oak of Ages,
at the same time that Orion was
invested with the Aspects of
Kurnous. Thus, the magical force
of nature flows through Ariel as
if she were the goddess Isha
herself.
Ariel wields the immense forces
of nature and directs them
according
to
her
will.
She
commands the trees of the forest
to grow, and the vegetation to
spring from the ground. It is
Ariel who casts enchantments all
around Athel Loren to delay
and destroy intruders, or lead
them straight to their doom. If
Ariel perishes in battle, the elves
will transport her and place her
in the Oak of Ages where she will
be reborn in spring.
When enemies enter Athel Loren, Ariel
takes on the Warrior Aspect of a sylph. She
grows to twice the size of an ordinary elf,
and spreads immense butterfly-like wings,
covered in tiny scales of iridescent colours.
On her wings appear the strange markings
known as the Eyes of Isha, and the Spirals
of Isha can also be seen in the patterns of
her wings. Sometimes Ariel's wings display
the markings of the deadly bombyx to
indicate that she is furious and in a
vengeful mood. Antennae emerge from
Ariel's head, but her face remains that of a
beautiful elf with piercing eyes. The upper
part
of
its
body
is
surrounded
by
shimmering scales of incandescent green,
while the lower part is lost in infinity - like
an ethereal or elemental being. She seems
to shine with

34
small bands of his people are based in many of
these forests, even without the knowledge of the
people who have rights to the land where they
are located. There is a good chance that this is
true, not only to serve as lookouts but also to
protect the dryads and treemen who may live
there. Or the real reason is that they are not
there to protect the spirits of the forest but
rather to monitor the actions of Drycha and her
followers.
Regardless, the men of Skarloc are known to
have unexpectedly changed the fate of many
battles, even in very distant lands, emerging
from the woods screaming like fiends to
hunt down and exterminate orcs or other evil
creatures.
Aside from Skarloc, the company brings together
three other personalities whose stories are
fabulous. Glam is the regiment's Bladesinger, a
fearless guardian of the forest paths. He is
renowned as one of the greatest Wardancers and
it is said that only Skarloc can control him. Many
stories are told about his wild youth: rumour has
it that he joined the archers after being kicked
out by his family who could no longer stand his
ferocity. He sports a huge crest of red hair coated
in
grease
which
makes
him
proud
and
intimidates the opponent. He is known to his
friends and foes alike as "the Laugher", because
in the heat of battle, while leaping and crossing
the
battlefield,
he
laughs
with
joy
and
exhilaration in combat, almost disdainfully
killing his opponents. His wild howl is often the
last thing Loren's enemies hear when they are
taken by surprise by Skarloc's company, their
remains joining those of countless others.
Kaia is a beautiful young elf, daughter of a
powerful mage. In search of adventure and
despite her father's disagreement, she joins the
wandering company of Skarloc. She holds high
the Standard of the Valiant Heart. This archaic
and highly respected totem is a holy relic
containing the ashes of the Heart of Kern, the
patron and inspiration of the Archers of Skarloc.
Both a mage and standard-bearer of the
regiment, she is known as the “Storm Witch” or
simply Kaia of Storms, bringing death and
destruction to the enemies of the Wood Elves.
Finally, Araflame the Skald has a large bronze
war horn, Carynx, whose sound strikes the
hearts of enemies with amazement.
Skarloc the Hooded is known far beyond Loren
Forest. He is originally from Laurelorn, which he
and his band of scouts, called the Archers of
Skarloc, left for obscure reasons. Little is known
about these archers. Their commander, Skarloc,
is a mysterious character who attracts many
young and idealistic elves under his banner.
Since his arrival in Loren, he seems to have
enjoyed the graces of the King and Queen of the
Forests, who offered him the Hail of Doom Arrow and
gave him the honorary title of Strider of the
Mists of Athel Loren. Since then he is also
sometimes called Scarloc even if only the King
and Queen know the real reasons. In Elvish, this
spelling change has the effect of making the
pronunciation of his name much more strident
than before.
At the head of the archers, he often ventures far
into the lands surrounding Athel Loren in order
to try to prevent in advance any possible threats
against the kingdoms of the Wood Elves. The
Archers of Skarloc have also taken upon
themselves the task of defending the forest and
the animals against the depredations of other
races. Although the primary targets of their
guerrilla attacks are goblinoids, they have been
known to hunt human settlers who have
ventured too deep into the forest. The exploits of
the Archers of Skarloc remain legendary, as for
example in 2007 of the Imperial Calendar, where
once again the monstrous Cyanathair died
pierced by hundreds of arrows fired by Skarloc
and his skilful scouts, or a laurëlornalim legend
which claims that thanks to him, out of two
hundred orcs of the Split Skulls tribe who
entered the forest, none ever came out!
Skarloc knows how to interpret tracks, traces
and all the signs of nature and he sometimes
warns the Bretonnians if he notices signs of
their common enemies. He has thus become
friends with many Bretonnian barons and is
always welcome in their castles, especially if he
brings with him Loren's excellent venison! It is
usually Skarloc who serves as an emissary for
the King and Queen of the Forests and it is he
who escorts their allies deep into the forest to
the Royal Glade.
Skarloc not only knows the smallest details of
every tree and path in Athel Loren, but also
every other forest in the Old World that he has
traveled over and over again on reconnaissance
missions. It is even claimed that

It is said that the first of all these
Chevaliers-Moires is Sacremor, the Green
Knight himself, in reality the spirit of Gilles
le Breton whom the Lady first elected to be
her herald and guardian. When Gilles
returned to the throne during the End
Times, and the flower of Bretonnia left to help
the Empire, leaving only the Grail Knights
to protect its holy places, an entire army of
spirit knights materialized during each of
Gilles' battles to let him direct the Lady's fury
against Chaos.
When Lileath confessed that she was the
Lady of the Lake, the last warriors of
Bretonnia turned away from her, but the
Chevaliers-Moires, faithful to their oath for
eternity, continued to fight the Chaos
which assailed Haven and to fight
alongside Gilles to save what remained of
Bretonnia.

The Chevaliers-Moires are the guardians of
Haven, this world created by Lileath with the
help of Eldyra, the heir of Ereth Kial, to
protect her precious daughter during the End
Times.
Since the founding of Bretonnia, the Lady of
the Lake had collected the souls of the
knights who perished in her service, and
hidden these spirits beneath the surface of
the mirror lakes, where the spirit of the Lady
was most powerful. Alongside these knights,
she also placed the spirits of the stolen
children of Bretonnia who were taken by the
Lady during their youth because they
possessed latent magical powers.
During his Quest for the Grail, young
Louen crossed a mirror lake and found
himself beneath its surface, invaded by the
grace of the Lady. He resurfaced at the
head of an army of Chevaliers-Moires in order
to destroy his enemies. Once the battle was
over, the spirits evaporated.

Equipment: The Dolorous Blade, the Silver Lance of the Blessed, Armour of the Green Knight, shield, Crown of Bretonnia, and barding.

Mount: The Shadow Steed comes from the world of the Lady's Mists and suffers no movement penalty for wearing barding.

The Crown of Bretonnia (Enchanted Item): No one knows the smith who made the Crown, for the Lady herself gave it to Gilles millennia ago. This ancient symbol of authority passed unbroken from king to king before returning to Gilles in 2522. Allied units may use the King's Leadership within 18". A unit with line of sight to the King is also Immune to Psychology.

The Dolorous Blade (Magic Weapon): This unique blade, adorned with floral motifs, shimmers with a magical aura and is not of this world. In each close combat phase, Gilles may use it to gain either +D6 Attacks or +2 Strength.

The Silver Lance of the Blessed (Magic Weapon): Forged by Gilles, it can be wielded only by a knight with a pure heart. Attacks made with the lance hit automatically. Successful armour and ward saves against them must be re-rolled.

Armour of the Green Knight (Magic Armour): Forged by the fey, this armour protects the King as though the Lady had placed part of her power within it. Gilles has Magic Resistance (2).

Special Rules

Knight of the Haven: As the former Green Knight, King Gilles retains a supernatural, magical essence. In battle he seems imbued with ancient magic and does not fear mortal blades. He has the Ethereal, Terror, Unbreakable, and Unstable special rules. Gilles may join or leave any Bretonnian unit despite being Ethereal.

Grail Vow: Gilles le Breton has taken the Grail Vow.

Virtue of the Monster Slayer: Gilles fought and defeated many beasts that haunted the Massif Orcal, including a great drake. Their heads became trophies upon his fortress walls. Gilles has the Heroic Killing Blow special rule.

Lady's Blessing: Gilles always benefits from the Lady's Blessing, giving him a 5+ ward save whether or not the army prayed.

Aura of the Fay: Gilles is more than a mortal; his soul remains linked to the Lady's Haven, beyond mortal ideas of life and death. If his Wounds are reduced to 0, he disappears. Roll a D6: on a 3+, he returns beside a forest or natural terrain feature in the Bretonnian player's next Movement phase. The required roll rises to 4+, then 5+, then 6+ each time he disappears again. If the roll fails, he is slain for the rest of the battle.

Beloved King of Bretonnia: Gilles must be the army's General. If he is slain after failing to return, every Bretonnian unit must take a Panic test and becomes Stubborn.

Mallobaude was already uncompromising
during his lifetime, and cruel after receiving
the Blood Kiss. After his coronation, he
became despotic. The last dukes and barons
still loyal to the ideals of chivalry were
mercilessly hunted down and killed by the
minions of the Vampire King, and the feeble
attempts of Bretonnia's historic allies - the
Asrai as well as a few small armed forces
from the Empire and Estalia - already
severely
tested
by
the
war,
were
systematically
repulsed.
Mallobaude
immediately enslaved the entire population,
installed his own dynasty of vampires on the
ducal thrones, violently suppressed any
revolt, including those of his own offspring,
and bathed his reign in blood.

Mallobaude the Dragon, Vampire King of Bretonnia is an unofficial character, representing Mallobaude after he has
become King. He can be added, after your opponent's agreement, to any army of Mousillon, Vampire Counts or
Legions of Undeath and counts as a Lord's choice. He must be taken as presented here, and has no options.
Modifying his coat of arms with the image of
one of the last dragons of Bretonnia which
he killed and had brought to life by his
necromancers to make it his mount, he
became Mallobaude the Dragon, the first
Vampire King of Bretonnia, slayer of Chaos.
The Norscan ships that landed in the years
that followed were thrown back into the sea;
the herds of beastmen which were emerging
in ever greater numbers from the woods
were destroyed and reanimated in order
to better counter those that followed; the
rifts in reality that spewed Daemons into the
blackened lands of Bretonnia were closed by
necromancers
through
bloody
rituals.
Through his iron fist, Mallobaude succeeded
where Vlad and Mannfred failed to create a
kingdom of undeath.
Magic Mallobaude is a level 1
wizard who can use one of the
following Lores: Lore of Vampires,
Death, Shadow, or Undeath.
Magic Items The Crown of Bretonnia
(Enchanted Item) No one knows the
blacksmith who made the Crown of

Lady herself to Gilles millennia ago. This
ancient symbol of authority was passed
down through time uninterruptedly to
each new King until it was worn by the
Vampire King in 2522. Having become a
symbol of tyranny, even its sacred magic
seemed to be withered by its new owner.
Allied
troops
can
use
the
King's
Leadership within 18". An
Undead unit with line of sight on the King
loses one fewer Wound
when the Unstable rule is resolved.

The final battle of the Year
of Woe was the Siege
of Mousillon. The Tzeentch
Daemons
of
Kairos
were
searching for the last relic
located in the castle. Those
of Nurgle led by Ku'gath
aimed only to prevent the
destruction of the walled
city.
Finally,
Arkhan
believing that the Daemons
wanted to hinder his plans
to
resurrect
Nagash,
ordered Mallobaude to ensure the
Daemons be repelled at all
costs without letting them
enter the keep. At the
height of the assault, the
Bretonnian army attempted
a desperate sortie, just as
Ku'gath called in his troops.
A
complex
battle
then
began.
ARMIES Players agree in advance on the
value of armies. One of the armies is taken
from the Bretonnia army book. It must
contain
Mallobaude,
Black
Knight
of
Mousillon (see page 19). It represents only
50% of the chosen value. The second army is
a Chaos Daemon army. It must contain
Kairos Fateweaver, and cannot
contain any models bearing the Daemon
of Khorne, Daemon of Slaanesh, or Daemon of
Nurgle rules. The third army is an army of
Chaos Daemons. It must contain Ku'gath,
Plaguefather, and cannot contain any
models bearing the Daemon of Khorne,
Daemon of Slaanesh, or Daemon of Tzeentch
rules.
SETUP The game table is set up according
to the diagram opposite. Place the
terrain features outside the fortress following
the usual rules, except that the Bretonnian
deployment zone cannot contain any
terrain features (it is an open space in front of
the castle). Mallobaude's army is deployed
first. War machines must be deployed in
the fortress, missile units can be
deployed in the fortress. All other units, as
well as Mallobaude, must be deployed
outside the fortress. Once the army of
Mallobaude is deployed, place the army of
Kairos then that of Ku'gath. FIRST
TURN The first turn is played in this
order: 1. Army of Kairos 2. Army of
Ku'gath 3. Army of Mallobaude The order
of play during the following turns is
determined according to the rules of the
Triumph & Treachery supplement. Authors:
Ilmarith, with the help of Dreadaxe and
Thindaraïel.

The following pages present the rules for the campaign's unique scenarios. You can also reuse them outside this campaign by
adapting the forces involved, for example.
DAEMONIC ASSAULT ON MOUSILLON
45
DURATION OF THE GAME
The battle lasts 6 turns.
SPECIAL RULES
Multiplayer Battle (see Triumph & Treachery); No One Can
Be Trusted (see Triumph & Treachery, p. 16); Chaos
Ascendant: Tzeentch (see The End Times: Glottkin).
Fortress: If the fortress is used, also use Sharing Defensive
Units (see Blood in the Badlands, p. 89), Moving in the
Fortress, Shooting from the Fortress, and Attacking the
Fortress (p. 90).
Last Hope: This is Mallobaude's army's last chance for
victory. It makes a desperate sortie and leaves the fortress
gates open; they cannot be closed.
VICTORY CONDITIONS
The winner is determined by the opposing generals slain.
• Kairos's army scores 3 points if it kills Mallobaude and 1
point if it kills Ku'gath.
• Ku'gath's army scores 3 points if it kills Kairos and 1 point if
it kills Mallobaude.
• Mallobaude's army scores 1 point if Kairos is slain, plus 1
additional point if it delivers the killing blow. The same
applies to Ku'gath.
The winner is the army with the most points (each army can
score 0 to 4). If tied, use victory points as the tiebreaker.

SPECIAL RULES
Civil War (Bretonnia only; the Spirits are
unaffected).
The Briarmaven of Woe: At the start of
turn 3, the Wildwood Host enters through
the woods. Deploy each unit within 3" of a
wood and more than 6" from an enemy.
The Host may act normally. To represent its
treacherous purpose, at the start of each
Rebel turn roll a D6; on a 5+, the Rebel
player may use any unengaged Spirits as
part of their army. Engaged Spirits remain
unaffected and keep fighting.
Mannfred's Spoils: If a Host unit comes within 3"
of Morgiana, it abducts the Fay Enchantress, who
is removed from the table. The entire Host then
passes to the Rebel player's control. Host units
fighting Rebels immediately disengage and are
placed 1" away. If the unit carrying Morgiana
reaches a table edge or enters a Forest, it escapes
and she is permanently captured. If that unit is
destroyed first, place Morgiana back on the table
within 3" of its final position.
VICTORY CONDITIONS
Use the normal victory conditions for a pitched
battle.
Drycha's betrayal and Morgiana's
abduction do not alter the victory
conditions, but they greatly change
the balance of forces.

THE BATTLE OF QUENELLES - FATHER AND SON
51

At the centre of the battlefield, father and illegitimate son finally face one another. The Lion and the Serpent meet to settle their differences.

Note: If Mallobaude has not revealed himself:

  • Use the rules for Mallobaude the Black Knight instead of Mallobaude the Vampire Duke.
  • Use the Bretonnia army list instead of the Mousillon army list.
  • If Mallobaude is defeated, his army takes Panic tests in the same way as the Loyalists if Louen is defeated.
  • Use the Bretonnia army list instead of the Alliance Against Undeath.
  • Do not play the Flank Battle; ignore the Central Battle special rule.

The players agree in advance on the points value of the armies. The Rebel army is chosen from the Mousillon list and must include Mallobaude the Vampire Duke (see page 19). The Loyalist army is chosen from the Alliance Against Undeath list and must include King Louen and Duke Tancred (see page 13).

SETUP Use the Pitched Battle setup.

FIRST TURN The Rebel player takes the first turn.

GAME LENGTH The battle lasts 6 turns.

VICTORY CONDITIONS Determine the winner using the normal Pitched Battle victory conditions.

SPECIAL RULES

Civil War (Bretonnia).

The Throne is at Stake: If Louen is defeated in close combat, the Bretonnians lose heart and must immediately take a Panic test. They must then take another Panic test at the start of each of their turns until the battle ends. If Mallobaude is defeated, the Undead army loses cohesion and must immediately take an Instability test, then another at the start of each of its turns.

Clash of Leaders: Louen and Mallobaude each gain one additional Movement step when moving directly towards one another.

Central Battle: The third battle begins normally. Reinforcements from the other two battlefields then arrive. From the 3rd turn, the active player rolls one D6 for each reinforcement unit during the Remaining Moves sub-phase. On a 5+, that unit may enter the battlefield using the Reinforcements rule. When the first unit arrives, its player chooses one short table edge; every unit from that battle enters from that edge. Units from the other battle enter from the opposite edge.

Units that have lost models do not recover them and arrive at their current strength. Likewise, wounded characters do not recover Wounds. Abilities and special rules that may be used once per battle, such as a Dragon's Breath weapon, are recharged and may be used during the central battle.

Authors: Ilmarith and Thindaraiel, with help from Dreadaxe.

troops in the assault on
Maisontaal. In reality, this
has been his objective for
more than two centuries,
and
the
success
of
his
protégé finally allows him to
attack
the
fortified

Play the paired scenarios The Battle of

ATTACK ON LA MAISONTAAL
52
Heinrich Kemmler pledged
allegiance to Chaos long ago.
Tzeentch, sensing Nagash's
return, ordered him to steal
Alakanash,
Nagash's
sceptre, in order to block the
return
of
the
Great
Necromancer. But Arkhan,
the loyal vizier of Nagash,
was not going to let him.
ARMIES Players agree in advance on the
value of armies, which must not exceed 500
points. The first army is taken from the
Vampire
Counts
army
list.
Heinrich
Kemmler is added free of charge. The second
army is taken from the Vampire Counts
army list. Arkhan the Black is added for free.
SETUP The table is very small, representing
the crypt of the abbey. It is a 60 x 60 cm table,
with a flat floor, cluttered with debris (the
masonry of the roof collapsed following the
attack on the abbey). On one side there is the
door to the stairs that lead to the crypt. In
the middle of the other 3 sides there is a
chest. Kemmler's army is deployed first, in
the centre of the table. It cannot be within 5"
of a chest. Arkhan's army is deployed from
the gate. It cannot be closer to a chest than
Kemmler's army. It cannot come within 4" of
Kemmler's army (Kemmler's army must
move forward to make room. The scenario
begins when both armies are fully deployed).
FIRST
TURN
The
player
playing
Kemmler goes first. DURATION OF THE
GAME The battle lasts 5 turns. SPECIAL
RULES Civil War (Vampire Counts). You
can also (but it is not obligatory) use the
Warbands rules. The Crypt of Secrets: If a
unit reaches a chest, it opens it. Roll 1D6,
on a 5+ it contains Alakanash, otherwise it
contains a Ring of Cursed Fire. When a
unit reaches the 2nd chest, it contains
Alakanash on a 4+, otherwise it contains a
Sword of Might. The 3rd chest must contain
Alakanash. Alakanash: Only Kemmler and
Arkhan can carry Alakanash. They must
therefore reach the chest where the object
is located to take it. They can then move
around with it. VICTORY CONDITIONS If
Kemmler or Arkhan is killed, his opponent
immediately wins the game. If Kemmler
or Arkhan holds Alakanash and reaches
the crypt door, he immediately wins.
Otherwise, the winner is the one who
possesses Alakanash at the end. If neither
has found Alakanash before the end of the
5th turn, it is a draw. Authors:
Thindaraïel, with the help of Dreadaxe
and Ilmarith.
DUEL OF NECROMANCERS
53
Finally
the
army
of
Mallobaude, having crushed
those of most of the loyalist
duchies, presented itself at
the gates of Couronne. The
throne was within reach of
Mallobaude,
its
previous
occupant now gone. The last
loyal
dukes
had
hastily
gathered what troops they
had left, and at their head
was Sacremor, the Green
Knight, alone embodying
the hope of the Lady of the
Lake
to
bring
peace
to
Bretonnia. Mallobaude, as
he had become accustomed
to doing since his victory at
Quenelles, challenged the
army to a duel, certain of his
victory. But it was Sacremor
who took up the gauntlet…
ARMIES Players agree in advance on the
value of armies. The Rebel army is taken
from the Mousillon army list, and must
include Mallobaude the Vampire Duke. It
has +50% points compared to the agreed
value (for example, for a battle decided at
2000 points, the Rebel army actually has
3000 points). The Loyalist army is taken
from the Bretonnia book, and must include
the Green Knight. SETUP The game table is
set up for a siege. The armies are deployed in
the usual order (except Mallobaude and
Sacremor, see the Duel to the Death rule)
FIRST TURN The Loyalist player goes first.
DURATION OF THE GAME The battle lasts
6 turns.
SPECIAL RULES Duel to the Death:
Sacremor and Mallobaude are not placed
at the same time as their armies. They are
deployed in the centre of the table in
base-to-base contact. In the first round of
melee, they are both considered to have
charged. The two fighters are Unbreakable
for the duration of the duel. No unit can
intervene in the duel, they cannot be
charged or targeted (spell, shot, etc.).
VICTORY CONDITIONS If Mallobaude or
Sacremor
dies,
the
game
ends
immediately and his opponent is declared
the winner. If at the end of the 6th turn,
neither duelist is dead, count victory
points as usual. In the event of a tie, it is
the numerical superiority of the Rebels
that decides the result, and they win the
game. Authors: Ilmarith.
THE BATTLE OF COURONNE
54
The Serpent returned to his
hole, pursued by his father
the Lion. Mallobaude watches
his army disintegrating little
by little, his allies betraying
him in the hope of a possible
royal pardon, and he now
takes refuge in his castle.
Louen
Leoncoeur
is
determined to put an end to
the “Mousillon problem”,
the thorn in the side of the
Bretonnian
kings
for
centuries.
After
having
extensively bombarded the
castle, and having ensured
that not a single person
remains alive inside, it is
time for him to launch an
attack to drive out the dead.
ARMIES Players agree in advance on the
value of armies. The Rebel army is taken
from the Vampire Counts army list. It must
contain Mallobaude the Vampire Duke, as
well as a unit of Black Grail Knights. It
cannot contain Kemmler, Krell or Arkhan.
The Loyalist army is taken from the
Bretonnia book, and must include Louen
the Lionheart. SETUP The game table
represents the surroundings of Mousillon
Castle. So you need a fortress. The Loyalist
army is deployed first, then the Rebel army
is deployed in full.
FIRST TURN The Loyalist player goes
first. DURATION OF THE GAME The
battle lasts 6 turns. SPECIAL RULES
Siege (see Blood in the Badlands). The
Dead in the Walls: There are no more
living people in Mallobaude's army.
Therefore, no starvation rolls can be
made.
VICTORY
CONDITIONS
If
Mallobaude or Louen dies, the game ends
immediately and his opponent is declared
the winner. Otherwise, determine the
winner according to the usual siege rules.
THE SIEGE OF MOUSILLON
55
THE REVOLT OF MALLOBAUDE
Mallobaude the Serpent, bastard son of Louen Leoncoeur, takes up arms against his
father. He claims to know the truth about the Grail and the Lady, and vows to destroy
this false faith. Civil war rages as the dukes turn upon one another. Yet in the darkness,
the Serpent's sinister allies prepare a still darker plot-one intended to return a
terrifying figure to the world.
The Revolt of Mallobaude is a Warhammer campaign set on the eve of the End Times.
It may be played as a self-contained campaign with several possible endings, or linked
to the official End Times campaign books to reshape the fate of Bretonnia.
THIS BOOK CONTAINS
• Profiles and rules for the characters and
armies of the civil war;
• Scenarios and general rules for Civil War
battles and the key engagements of the Revolt.
RULES FOR WARHAMMER 8TH EDITION
